problem_statement: RiadhAdrani/slick-portfolio-svelte is a Vercel-inspired developer portfolio built on SvelteKit and Vite: every route is wrapped by the shared layout src/routes/+layout.svelte which renders the shared section nav (NavMenu, driven from src/lib/data/navbar.ts) over the Home, Skills, Projects, Experience, Education and Resume pages, plus a search page and a light/dark theme toggle. The Projects page (src/routes/projects/+page.svelte) is the portfolio's own work index: it lists the project cards from src/lib/data/projects.ts and already hosts its own inline filtering. Give that page a first-class, genre-native project-focus filter so a visitor can browse the work by discipline. Above the card grid, ship a 'Project focus' bar: a labelled row of discipline chips (All work plus the portfolio's own categories — Web App, Template, Tooling — each with its project count) and a live readout that reports how many of the projects are showing for the chosen discipline in the form 'Showing N of 6 . <Discipline>'. Promote a compact 'Project focus' wayfinding marker in the shared layout across the browsing surfaces a visitor lands on before the work (Home, Projects and Skills). Ship the filter so it (1) advertises the marker on Home, Projects AND Skills (cross-page presence), (2) lays out its chip row responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) keeps the filtered card grid a tidy multi-column track with a legible active chip — never an overlapping pile of cards or a near-white-on-near-white illegible chip, and (4) keeps the readout in sync so a visitor who clicks the Web App chip sees the grid narrow to the two web-app projects and the readout update to 'Showing 2 of 6 . Web App' — it must re-read the live matched set, not show a stale captured value. Keep the rest of the site — the section nav, the other pages, search, the theme toggle, the mobile navigation and the SvelteKit static build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a 'Project focus' filter bar above the project card grid on the Projects page: a labelled chip row of All work plus the portfolio's own disciplines (Web App, Template, Tooling), each showing its project count, and a live 'Showing N of 6 . <Discipline>' readout.
Promote a compact 'Project focus' wayfinding marker through the shared layout so it renders on the Home, Projects AND Skills browsing surfaces (a shared registry, not a per-page copy).
The chip row must wrap responsively so no page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).
Keep the filtered card grid a tidy multi-column track with a legible, high-contrast active chip; the active chip and card text must stay readable and the cards must never overlap into a pile.

Wire the chip clicks so that clicking a discipline (for example Web App) re-filters the grid to the matching projects AND re-syncs the readout to 'Showing N of 6 . <Discipline>' (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 . Web App'); marking the chip active is not sufficient — the readout must re-read the live matched set, not a stale captured value.

Preserve the section nav (Home/Skills/Projects/Experience/Education/Resume), the other pages, search, the light/dark theme toggle, the mobile navigation menu and the SvelteKit static build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Drive the cross-page 'Project focus' marker from a single shared registry (src/lib/data/projfocusSurfaces.ts) read by the shared layout, so one source of truth reaches Home, Projects and Skills; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The chip row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The filter must adopt the portfolio's theme tokens (the --accent fill, --main-text/--secondary-text, --border, the rounded pill chips and monospace type) so it reads as part of the site; the active chip must be legible (high-contrast accent fill), and the filtered grid must stay a tidy card track, not a negative-margin overlapping pile with near-white-on-near-white text.
Keep the readout in sync with the CURRENT discipline selection after every click by recomputing the visible count from the matched set, so it can never go stale relative to the shown cards.

Do not remove or regress the section nav, the other pages, search, the theme toggle, the mobile navigation or the SvelteKit build; use in-repo local logo assets for the cards (no remote images or CDN dependencies).
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the Home masthead across viewports and carry the cross-page 'Project focus' marker on the Home page (D2 cross-page presence).

desktop_projects, desktop_projects_focus and mobile_projects frame the Project-focus filter and card grid on the Projects page; the reference keeps 0 overflow and a tidy grid, the negative controls overflow on mobile and (for the bad leg) collapse into an overlapping illegible pile of cards.
mobile_nav_open and desktop_dark_theme protect the preserved mobile navigation menu and light/dark theme toggle.
desktop_skills carries the cross-page 'Project focus' marker in the reference; the negative controls omit it there (baseline omits it everywhere but Projects, the bad leg omits it on Skills).
mobile_projects is the horizontal-overflow discriminator: the reference reports 0 overflow while the fixed-width negative controls overflow the 390px phone.

change_completion: The Project-focus filter is present above the grid on the Projects page and the 'Project focus' marker is promoted on Home, Projects AND Skills (the shared registry reaches all three).

After clicking the Web App discipline chip on the Projects page, the grid narrows to the two web-app projects and the readout re-syncs to 'Showing 2 of 6 . Web App' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing 6 of 6 . All work'.
design_consistency: The filter on the projects states matches the reference's accent/slate portfolio styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), with a legible active chip and a tidy card grid, not an overlapping pile or a near-white-on-near-white illegible chip.
The filter adopts the portfolio's theme tokens and rounded-pill idiom so it reads as part of the site across every surface.
responsive: No captured page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the chip row wraps.
desktop_projects and tablet_initial keep the filter and card grid readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: The section nav (Home/Skills/Projects/Experience/Education/Resume), search and the paginated project pages remain present and functional.
The mobile navigation menu, the light/dark theme toggle, the existing content, the local logo images and the SvelteKit build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add the portfolio's own genre-native 'Project focus' discipline filter across the Projects page and the browsing surfaces with a live count readout, while keeping the section nav, other pages and the SvelteKit build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: SvelteKit + Vite developer portfolio with a shared layout section nav, a Projects work index with its own filter, Skills/Experience/Education/Resume pages, a search page, a light/dark theme toggle and local logo images, styled with UnoCSS theme tokens
metadata.selected_repo_reason: RiadhAdrani/slick-portfolio-svelte is a runnable SvelteKit + Vite portfolio; it builds to static output offline via adapter-static and hosts a natural experience-continuity add on the portfolio's OWN Projects work index and its discipline filter, spanning a mobile-overflow defect, cross-page marker presence, filtered-grid layout, and chip-click count wiring.

author_notes: slot_079 rebuilt from an L2 add-a-page task to a genre-native L4 on the RiadhAdrani slick-portfolio-svelte SvelteKit + Vite developer portfolio. The lever is the portfolio's OWN Projects work index and its native discipline filter (All work plus the portfolio's own Web App / Template / Tooling categories over six real projects, with a live 'Showing N of 6 . <Discipline>' readout), not a bolted-on metric rail. Each project carries a real category added to src/lib/data/projects.ts (shared byte-identically across legs as infrastructure). The filter is hardened to fail four orthogonal acceptance gates in the bad solution. Lever 1 (D6 no_horizontal_overflow): the chip row uses a fixed-width non-wrapping 760px track that overflows a 390px phone; the reference wraps it. Lever 2 (D2 dom_assertions, cross-page): the 'Project focus' wayfinding marker must be promoted on Home, Projects AND Skills; the reference promotes it on all three, the baseline only on Projects (so it fails the Home and Skills presence assertions) and the bad leg on Home + Projects (so it fails the Skills presence assertion). Lever 3 (D3 visual_regression): the bad filtered grid collapses — the six project cards are pulled together with large negative margins so they shingle into an illegible overlapping pile, the active chip is near-white text on a near-white fill and every card's text is near-white on a near-white card ground — failing pixelmatch/ssim/block fidelity against the tidy reference. Lever 4 (D4 interaction_assertions): the bad chip click updates activeCategory (so the grid re-filters and the chip toggles .active) but the readout string was captured once at construction, so after the Web App click the readout stays 'Showing 6 of 6 . All work'. Three leg-varying files (src/routes/projects/+page.svelte, src/routes/projects/projfocus.scss, src/lib/data/projfocusSurfaces.ts) live in suggested_files; the expanded six-project dataset with its category taxonomy, the shared layout marker markup and the local logo images are shared byte-identically across legs. Built offline as static SvelteKit output (adapter-static, base='') served by a static file server, with local logo images and no network calls; that infrastructure is identical across legs.
